newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatargas, Chubu extend interim price deal to June.
newsitem.headline: Qatargas, Chubu extend interim price deal to June.

text.p: Qatargas and Japan's Chubu Electric Power Co extended their interim price deal of $4.10 per million British Thermal Unit (BTU) for gas delivered in Nagoya by three months to June 30, industry sources said on Saturday.
Japan's Chubu is the principal customer of the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company, or Qatargas.
"It has been decided to extend the original arrangement to allow the parties the time to search for a definite formula to determine prices in the future," a Qatari official said.

Qatargas began supplying liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Chubu under a 25-year sales-and-purchase agreement (SPA) in January. Pricing has been left to periodic reviews linked to the quarterly fluctuations in crude oil prices.

In January, the two parties agreed to a $4.10 per million BTU price for deliveries until March 31. But as oil prices weakened since the beginning of the year, Chubu said the LNG price should also be "marginally cut back to keep pace with the cost of the competing fuel", an industry source said.
"However, in the absence of a definite mechanism in the SPA to calculate the price escalation or reduction, the parties failed to arrive at an agreement," he said. The talks began on Sunday.
Qatargas is 65 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corp, 10 percent each by U.S. Mobil Corp and France's Total and 7.5 percent each by Japan's Marubeni and Mitsui.

In 1994, it signed an SPA with Chubu and seven Japanese utilities to supply them with six million tonnes of LNG annually for 25 years. While Chubu's supply of four million tonnes a year started in January, the other companies' two million tonnes a year will begin in mid-1998.
The SPA guarantees a minimum price of $3.60 per million BTU for gas delivered at Chubu's terminal at Kawagoe port in Nagoya.
